name: Sri Mahamariamman Temple, Penang
significance: The mother-goddess temple of George Town's Tamil quarter, begun as a shrine on land granted in 1801 and built up into a temple by 1833. It has been reconsecrated five times between 1933 and 2016, taking the honorific Arulmigu at the 1980 kumbabishekam.

name: Arulmigu Sri Rajakaliamman Glass Temple
significance: A Kaliamman temple in Johor Bahru that began in 1922 as a simple shelter and was rebuilt in 1996. Between 2008 and October 2009 its interior was sheathed in glasswork, giving it the name by which it is now known.

name: Arulmigu Maha Muthu Mariamman Thevasthanam
significance: A Perak temple founded in 1962 as a Kaliamman shrine, reordered in 1964 so that Mariamman became the principal deity, and registered under her name in 1967. A wholly new temple was begun in December 2006 and consecrated at its kumbabishekam in December 2010.
story: Devotees hold that the eagles which circled overhead during the 2010 kumbabishekam were Garuda, Vishnu's mount, marking the new temple with divine assent.

name: Jalan Baru Sri Muniswarar Temple
significance: One of the older Tamil shrines on the Penang mainland, set up in the 1870s by Indian labourers who came with the East India Company. It opened as Sri Muniandy Temple and was later renamed for Muniswarar, the village guardian deity worshipped at its main altar alongside Ganesha and Murugan.
story: The guardian is said to ride the neighbourhood after midnight on a white horse with an arivaal blade and a cigar, and a Chinese devotee who saw him enter the temple grounds so mounted paid for an altar in his honour.

name: Arulmigu Karumariamman Temple
significance: A temple to the rural South Indian mother goddess Karumariamman that descends from an estate shrine serving Paduma Estate workers at Perai and was moved when Seberang Jaya township was laid out in the 1970s. The present RM2.3 million building was started in 1996, with the works minister S. Samy Vellu laying its foundation stone on 16 February 1997.
